stem.text: Secondary amine M can be made by the three-step synthesis shown in Figure 8.1.

stem.caption: Figure 8.1
stem.alt: CH3COOH, step 1, CH3COCl, step 2, an empty box labelled L; step 3 (downward arrow) gives M, CH3CH2-NH-CH(CH3)2.

stem.text: Write an equation for the reaction of CH3COOH with SOCl2 in step 1.

explanation.text: Thionyl chloride replaces the –OH of the carboxylic acid with –Cl. The by-products SO<sub>2</sub> and HCl are both gases, which escape and leave the acyl chloride behind.
Acyl chlorides react with water, so adding ‘(aq)’ to any species contradicts the answer (CON).

reasoningChain: Replace OH in CH<sub>3</sub>COOH by Cl to get CH<sub>3</sub>COCl.
The remaining atoms (S, O, Cl, H) form SO<sub>2</sub> + HCl.
Check the balance: C2 H4 O3 S Cl2 on each side.

inferredMistakes.text: Writing H<sub>2</sub>O or SOCl as a product, so the equation does not balance.
Adding state symbol (aq), which the MS treats as contradictory.

stem.text: State an alternative reagent that reacts with CH3COOH to produce CH3COCl in step 1.

guidance: A names, phosphorus(III) chloride, phosphorus trichloride, phosphorus(V) chloride, phosphorus pentachloride.
CON aq, but not in both 8(a)(i) and 8(a)(ii).

explanation.text: The syllabus lists three reagents that turn a carboxylic acid into an acyl chloride: PCl<sub>3</sub> with heat, PCl<sub>5</sub>, or SOCl<sub>2</sub>. Step 1 used SOCl<sub>2</sub>, so either phosphorus chloride is the alternative.

reasoningChain: Recall the three chlorinating reagents for carboxylic acids.
Give one that is not SOCl<sub>2</sub>: PCl<sub>3</sub> or PCl<sub>5</sub>.

inferredMistakes.text: Giving HCl or Cl<sub>2</sub>, which do not convert a carboxylic acid into an acyl chloride.
Giving an aqueous reagent; the MS penalises (aq), though only once across (a)(i) and (a)(ii).

stem.text: Draw the structure of L in Figure 8.1.

guidance: Or any unambiguous structural or skeletal formula.
markScheme.note: The MS prints a drawn structural formula followed by ‘or CH3CONHCH(CH3)2’.

figure.alt: Structure of L from the MS: CH3C(=O)-NH-CH(CH3)2.

explanation.text: Work backwards from M. Step 3 must be the reduction of an amide C=O to CH<sub>2</sub> (LiAlH<sub>4</sub>), so L has the same skeleton as M with C=O in place of the CH<sub>2</sub> next to N. M is CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>–NH–CH(CH<sub>3</sub>)<sub>2</sub>; the CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub> part came from CH<sub>3</sub>CO, so L is CH<sub>3</sub>CO–NH–CH(CH<sub>3</sub>)<sub>2</sub>, N-(propan-2-yl)ethanamide.

reasoningChain: The acyl part of L comes from CH<sub>3</sub>COCl, so L contains CH<sub>3</sub>CO–N.
Match the rest to M: the N also carries CH(CH<sub>3</sub>)<sub>2</sub>.

inferredMistakes.text: Drawing the amide on the wrong side, e.g. CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>NHCOCH<sub>3</sub>, which could not come from CH<sub>3</sub>COCl and the isopropyl amine.
Drawing M itself or the amine instead of the amide.

stem.text: Draw the structure of the reagent added to CH3COCl in step 2.

guidance: No ecf from 8(a)(iii) – Q specifies L is an amide and gives the structure of M.
markScheme.note: The MS prints a structural formula ‘or CH3CHNH2CH3’; the Guidance column adds an accepted skeletal formula. Both drawings are in the figure.

figure.alt: From the MS: left, H2N-CH(CH3)2 drawn as a structural formula; right, from the Guidance column, the accepted skeletal formula of propan-2-amine (NH2 on the middle carbon of a three-carbon chain).

explanation.text: An acyl chloride reacts with a primary amine at room temperature to give an N-substituted amide and HCl. Since L is CH<sub>3</sub>CONHCH(CH<sub>3</sub>)<sub>2</sub>, the amine must be propan-2-amine, (CH<sub>3</sub>)<sub>2</sub>CHNH<sub>2</sub>.

reasoningChain: Split L at the amide C–N bond: CH<sub>3</sub>CO– came from CH<sub>3</sub>COCl.
The other half, –NHCH(CH<sub>3</sub>)<sub>2</sub>, came from the amine H<sub>2</sub>NCH(CH<sub>3</sub>)<sub>2</sub>.

inferredMistakes.text: Drawing propan-1-amine, CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>NH<sub>2</sub>, which would not give the branched M.
Drawing ethylamine, by reading the CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub> group of M as the amine part.

stem.text: Name the mechanism of the reaction forming L in step 2.

guidance: No ecf from 8(a)(iii) – Q specifies L is an amide.

explanation.text: The lone pair on the amine N attacks the δ+ carbonyl carbon of CH<sub>3</sub>COCl (addition), then the C=O reforms and Cl<sup>–</sup> leaves, followed by loss of H<sup>+</sup> (elimination). The mechanism is addition–elimination.
‘Condensation’ describes the overall reaction (two molecules join and lose HCl), not the mechanism, so it is ignored.

reasoningChain: The amine acts as a nucleophile on the C=O carbon (addition).

inferredMistakes.text: Writing only ‘condensation’, which names the reaction type, not the mechanism.

guidance: No ecf from 8(a)(iii) – Q specifies L is an amide.

explanation.text: Step 3 reduces the amide C=O to CH<sub>2</sub>, turning L into the secondary amine M. LiAlH<sub>4</sub> is the syllabus reagent for reducing amides to amines. It reacts violently with water, so it is used in dry ether, and ‘(aq)’ contradicts it.

reasoningChain: Compare L and M: C=O has become CH<sub>2</sub>, which is a reduction.
Choose the reagent for reducing an amide: LiAlH<sub>4</sub>.

inferredMistakes.text: Giving NaBH<sub>4</sub>, which reduces aldehydes and ketones but not amides.
Giving H<sub>2</sub>/Ni, which the syllabus uses for nitriles, not amides.

stem.text: The proton (1H) NMR spectrum of M dissolved in D2O is obtained. Four of the proton environments, r, s, t and u, are labelled on the structure of M in Figure 8.2.

stem.caption: Figure 8.2
stem.alt: Structure of M, CH3CH2-NH-CH(CH3)2, with labels: r on the CH3 of the ethyl group, s on the CH2, u on the CH, and t on each of the two CH3 groups attached to the CH.

stem.text: Complete Table 8.1 to identify the splitting patterns for proton environments r, s, t and u.

guidance: ⚫✓⚫✓ two points for one mark, four points for two marks.

explanation.text: Use the n + 1 rule: a proton signal is split into n + 1 lines by n equivalent H atoms on the adjacent carbon(s). In D<sub>2</sub>O the N–H proton is exchanged for D, so it does not couple and the CH<sub>2</sub>/CH protons next to N are split only by protons on carbon.

r (CH<sub>3</sub> of ethyl): next to CH<sub>2</sub> (2 H), so 3 lines, a triplet. s (CH<sub>2</sub>): next to CH<sub>3</sub> (3 H), so a quartet. t (two equivalent CH<sub>3</sub>): next to one CH (1 H), so a doublet. u (CH): next to 6 H of two CH<sub>3</sub>, so 7 lines, a septet, which the syllabus calls a multiplet.

reasoningChain: For each environment, count the H atoms on neighbouring carbons (ignore N–H, exchanged in D<sub>2</sub>O).
Apply n + 1: r 2 → triplet; s 3 → quartet; t 1 → doublet; u 6 → 7 lines (multiplet).

inferredMistakes.text: Counting the N–H proton as a neighbour of s and u, which gives the wrong splitting for the CH<sub>2</sub> and CH.
Using n instead of n + 1, e.g. calling r a doublet and s a triplet.
Counting the two CH<sub>3</sub> groups (t) as neighbours of each other, giving a split other than a doublet.

stem.text: The proton (1H) NMR spectrum of M dissolved in CDCl3 is obtained.
State and explain how this spectrum differs from the proton (1H) NMR spectrum of M dissolved in D2O.

guidance: A ‘NH peak is not present in D2O’.
A reference to five peaks or five proton environments and reference to N-H.
A ‘it is exchanged with D’ if NH peak already referred to and you are confident they refer to ‘in D2O’.
A ‘it is not exchanged with D’ if NH peak already referred to and you are confident they refer to ‘in CDCl3’.

points.text:
M1 one more peak and reference to N-H
Subject of Q is ‘in CDCl3’ so assume this if no solvent specified.
See first two ALLOWs in guidance.

M2 H (of NH) is exchanged with D (in D2O) / NH + D → ND + H / H (of NH) is not exchanged with D (in CDCl3)
the bits in brackets for M2 are not essential but if clearly wrong it is CON

explanation.text: CDCl<sub>3</sub> is a deuterated solvent that has no exchangeable H, so the N–H proton of M stays as N–H and gives its own peak. In D<sub>2</sub>O the N–H proton exchanges with deuterium (N–H + D<sub>2</sub>O ⇌ N–D + HDO), and D does not appear in a <sup>1</sup>H spectrum, so the N–H peak disappears.
So the CDCl<sub>3</sub> spectrum has one more peak (five environments instead of four), and that extra peak is the N–H.

reasoningChain: Recall which proton in M is exchangeable: the N–H.
In D<sub>2</sub>O it becomes N–D, which gives no <sup>1</sup>H peak.
In CDCl<sub>3</sub> no exchange happens, so there is one extra (N–H) peak.

inferredMistakes.text: Saying ‘D<sub>2</sub>O replaces the H’, which the MS ignores: it is the H atom that is exchanged for a D atom.
Saying there is an extra peak without saying it is the N–H peak.
Getting the solvents the wrong way round, i.e. saying the N–H exchanges in CDCl<sub>3</sub>.

issues.note: MS 答案是画出的结构式 + 'or' 文字式。figure 放结构式图，文字式写成 point 的 alternative；point 正文是简短描述。8(a)(iv) 的 Guidance 'or skeletal' 后面是一张骨架式图，和答案图拼在同一张 figure 里（右侧）。

答案栏 M1 下方的 'Subject of Q is … See first two ALLOWs in guidance.' 和 M2 下方的 'the bits in brackets for M2 …' 是答案栏里的说明，用
接在对应 point 后面，没有移到 Guidance。
u（CH，邻接 6 个 H）严格按 n+1 是 septet；MS 写 multiplet，Guidance 也接受 septet/heptet/septuplet。与考纲 37.4(1) 'limited to singlet, doublet, triplet, quartet and multiplet' 一致，非错误，仅说明。
跨章题（29、33、34、37 章）。主线是用酰胺还原合成仲胺 M（34.1、34.3），放在第 34 章（Nitrogen compounds）。
